prose.text: A customer who wants their own addresses as the egress address may mean this or Source IP Anchoring. {{definition}} {{prerequisites}}

prose.label: Not Source IP Anchoring.
prose.text: {{not-sipa}} The anchoring mechanism is in [[zia.forwarding-control.sipa]]; a rule uses Dedicated IP addresses through the Dedicated IP method and gateway: [[zia.forwarding-control.methods]].

definition.statement: Zscaler's Dedicated IP service can use Zscaler-owned or customer-owned addresses; bringing your own range into the Zscaler cloud is called BYOIP.

quotes: Zscaler's dedicated IP service provides organizations with dedicated IP addresses and also allows you to bring your own IP address range (i.e., Bring Your Own IP or BYOIP) into the Zscaler cloud.

prerequisites.statement: BYOIP needs at least one /24 for each Zscaler data center where addresses are to be provisioned, a subscription to the dedicated IP service, a prefix registered with the Regional Internet Registry and associated with an ASN, and verification by a cryptographic Route Origin Authorization (ROA).

quotes: You require at least one /24 subnet for each Zscaler data center where you need dedicated IP addresses to be provisioned.
You must subscribe to the Zscaler dedicated IP service, which provisions dedicated IP addresses at a single Zscaler data center.
Customer-owned IP addresses must be verified using cryptographic Route Origin Authorization (ROA) for integration into Zscaler's dedicated IP service.

The IP address prefix must be registered with your Regional Internet Registry (RIR), which manages the allocation of numbered resources like IP addresses, and associated with an Autonomous System Number (ASN).

roa-asns.statement: The ROA names a Zscaler ASN by region: AS53813 for APAC, AS22616 for the Americas and AS62044 for EMEA; the ROA must be for the same prefix length as the prefix announced from the data center.

quotes: APAC: AS53813
Americas: AS22616
EMEA: AS62044
the ROA object must be the same prefix length that is announced from a data center.

signing.statement: The customer attaches a self-signed X.509 public certificate to the prefix's RIR record (comments for ARIN, remarks for RIPE and APNIC), then signs a message in the form <version>|<prefix>|<mesg_expire_date> with SHA-256 and RSA-PSS. Zscaler recommends an expiry at least one month after creating the message.

quotes: Create a self-signed x.509 certificate
attach the public certificate to your netblock where the BYOIP prefix is allocated, in the comment or remarks section of your RIR:
ARIN: Edit the comments of the prefix record
RIPE: Edit the remarks of the inetnum record
APNIC: Edit the remarks of the inetnum record
create a Zscaler BYOIP message with the following format: <version>|<prefix>|<mesg_expire_date>
openssl dgst -sha256 -sigopt rsa_padding_mode:pss
Zscaler recommends setting the expiration date at least one month ahead of creating the message

support-ticket.statement: Provisioning is requested through a Zscaler Support ticket naming the data centers and carrying the message and its signature; Support validates the routes, advertises them from the requested data centers and provisions addresses from the prefix to the tenant.

quotes: After signing your BYOIP message, submit a Zscaler Support ticket with the following information:
The list of Zscaler data centers where the IP prefixes need to be advertised.
The Zscaler BYOIP text message and signed message.
the Zscaler Support team validates the authenticity of the routes, advertises the routes from the requested data centers, and provisions the IP addresses from the prefix to your Zscaler tenant.

not-sipa.statement: BYOIP and Source IP Anchoring are different mechanisms: BYOIP brings a customer-owned, ROA-authorized prefix into the Dedicated IP service, while Source IP Anchoring makes the Private Access App Connector's address the source. Licensing and mechanism assumptions for one do not carry to the other.
not-sipa.conditions: Derived from the two features' own descriptions; no source compares them directly.
